text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed broadly higher in late afternoon trade after giving up earlier modest losses. The market had been weighed down by scale-up selling which capped the recent gains racked up on the front-month October contract. October finished unchanged at $328.00 after ranging between $326.80 and 328.40 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed firmer on mixed buying, market sources said. Steady trade selling in the spreads pressured the spot months to the day's low of 11.42 cents/lb where local short-covering stymied losses. Commission house buying carried the contract to the day's high of 11.57 cents/lb. Prices are expected to remain in the range between 11.40 to 11.65 cents/lb through Friday, and then could gradually creep higher.

However, open interest remains extremely high and this combined with a lack of bullish fundamental news makes prices vulnerable to a washout. October settled 0.07 cent firmer at 11.56 cents/lb, while the rest of the board finished 0.07 to 0.10 cent higher.

UNITED STATES - The USDA continues to adjust and fine-tune projections for fiscal year 1998 (October 1997/September 1998). In its July forecast the Department increased total sugar production by 75,000 short tons to 7.575 million tons, raw value. The new projection is 322,000 tons higher than FY 1997 sugar production. Higher cane production in Louisiana resulting from higher yielding sugar cane, accounts for the increase. Total sugar deliveries for FY 1998 are projected at 9.75 million short tons, a modest 100,000 tons above the FY 1997 result.

AUSTRIA - Sugar exports in June 1997 amounted to 13,394 tonnes, raw value, sharply up on 3,680 tonnes exported in June 1996. This brought cumulative exports in October/June 1996/97 up to 65,466 tonnes compared to 41,168 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 55,593 tonnes against 31,276 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Romania with 21,901 tonnes whites against 28,300 tonnes, Syria with 14,082 tonnes compared to nil and Mauritania with 8,602 tonnes against nil.

RUSSIA - The latest Russian beet test of July 20 showed a sugar content of 8.7 percent, down from 9.5 percent at the same time last year, the Rossakhsvyokla sugar beet producers association said. The root weight reached 136 g, up from 122 g in 1996. This would result in a theoretical sugar weight per root of 11.83 g, slightly up on the previous year's 11.59 g. Favourable weather resulted in a speedier root growth which reached 5.1 g per day compared to 4.6 g in 1996. Despite these positive results, it remains to be seen whether output will be higher given the fact that the area sown to beet dropped to 944,000 ha from over 1 million ha in 1996.

FINLAND - Sugar imports in April 1997 amounted to 10,402 tonnes which brought cumulative imports in October/April 1996/97 up to 20,372 tonnes compared to 1,257 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 48,087 tonnes against 52,647 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Brazil with 10,365 tonnes raws against nil and Fiji with 9,878 tonnes against nil. Sugar exports in October/April 1996/97 amounted to 21,709 tonnes compared to 34,078 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 were 49,721 tonnes, up from 6,763 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of destination in 1996/97 was Estonia with 9,733 tonnes whites against 8,076 tonnes.

Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) has re-issued a tender to buy 13,000 tonnes white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws, a GEZA spokesman said. He said August 5 was set as the final date to receive price offers and that the two amounts should be shipped in September. Results of the tender would be announced on August 6, it was added. GEZA passed on two previous tenders to buy the same quantity as price offers did not meet its conditions.
